summary.intent: Fix the oracle comparator so a checker-opaque type is no longer scored as `identical` (agreement), and consolidate duplicated verdict vocabulary and path-classification logic, then document it in PR #424.
summary.outcome: PR #424 (`fix/oracle-unjudged`, one signed commit, trail #303) now has its body written. It adds a `not judged` outcome, a typed `caliperNorm`, a shared vocabulary and path-class data, and an oracle typecheck. CI was not checked and `weekly.py --oracle` was not run.

repo: Oracle verdicts are defined once in `apps/oracle/src/vocabulary.ts` (VERDICTS, AGREE, SEVERITY, ROW_VERDICTS, OUTCOMES) and written to `vocabulary.json` via `pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle vocabulary`; `vocabulary.test.ts` fails if they differ, and Python reads it through `scripts/oracle_data.py`.

`@types/react` and `node_modules` path rules are shared via `path-classes.json`, with `path-class-cases.json` exercised by both `path-class.test.ts` and `test_path_classes.py`. Rust sites (about 60 `types/react` occurrences), directory-name pruning and display-only `shortFile` are intentionally not covered.

`weekly.py` `UNIVERSE_VERSION` must be bumped (3 to 4) when scoring semantics change. `shared_props`, `agree` and `wrong` formulas are unchanged, so a not-judged prop counts in `shared_props` but in neither `agree` nor `wrong`.
`headline.py` maps every verdict to one kind, so an unknown verdict raises `KeyError` instead of passing silently.
The oracle had no typecheck; `apps/oracle/tsconfig.json` and a `typecheck` script were added, which surfaced three existing type errors in `agent-truth.ts`.

Construct suite expectations live in `checker-expectations.json`; four rows (`generics/19-recursive-json`, `react/16-ref`, `react/27-sx-object`, `react/30-dispatch-setstate`) were reading `identical` against goldens truncated at the depth limit and are now `not judged`.
Validation commands: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just test-py`, `just test-checker-lane`, `just test-construct`, `python3 -m unittest` in `scripts/`.

code.finding: Single source of truth for verdict vocabulary; the old RANK became SEVERITY, the old ORDER became ROW_VERDICTS, and `GREEN` was deleted.
`caliperNorm` is now typed against its `PropType` via a type-only import, with a case per kind and a `never` exhaustiveness check; at runtime an unknown kind throws.

workflow: Verified the tests actually exercise the change by stashing it: 9 TS tests failed and 2 files couldn't import, 4 Python modules failed on import, and `UNIVERSE_VERSION` failed.
A clean-room run (oracle test, typecheck, Python tests, lint) was used as an extra check beyond the in-tree run.
The PR body was written with a heredoc to `$TMPDIR` and applied with `gh pr edit --body-file`.
The PR body explicitly separates what was verified from what wasn't, and the PR was kept as one commit because the files overlap too much to split.
